summary.one_liner: QuTiP is an open-source Python toolbox for simulating the dynamics of closed and open quantum systems, built on NumPy, SciPy, and Cython.
summary.what_it_does: QuTiP aims to provide user-friendly and efficient numerical simulations of quantum mechanical problems. It supports Hamiltonians and collapse operators with arbitrary time-dependence, which the README says are common in many physics applications. NumPy, SciPy, and Cython serve as numerical backends, and Matplotlib provides graphical output. The README describes it as free to use and modify, and suitable for research and teaching. Demonstration notebooks are kept in a separate qutip-tutorials repository. The README also points to a "How to work on an issue" guide for contributors.
use_cases: quantum mechanics teaching and classroom exercises
how_to_run: pip install qutip[full]  (installs all optional dependencies)
notable: Handles arbitrary time-dependent Hamiltonians and collapse operators
Free of licensing fees, usable for research and teaching
Documentation on Read The Docs and demo notebooks in a separate tutorials repository
caveats: README says it runs on Unix-based platforms and Windows; no other platform limits are stated
Building from source is covered only in the external detailed installation guide
